qa_pairs.question: Is the viral video/image showing PM Modi with a flag similar to the Pakistani national flag authentic?
qa_pairs.answer:
No, the viral image is not authentic. It has been identified as a fake, morphed image.

According to the evidence, the original photo was taken during the inauguration of the Bogibeel Bridge in Assam on December 25, where Prime Minister Modi was actually waving a plain green flag. Fact-checking research, including reverse image searches and verification via the Prime Minister's official website, confirmed that the white crescent and star (which make the flag resemble the Pakistani national flag) were subsequently superimposed onto the original image to create the misleading post.

questions.question: Were there any reports of the event in the pakistani parliament?

answers.answer: A detailed report of the proceedings are detailed in a report in the Dawn, there is no mention of people shouting Modi Modi. But people did shout 'voting, voting'

statements.statement: The video clip of the Pakistani parliamentary proceedings shows members chanting 'voting, voting' rather than 'Modi, Modi', including a 17 minutes 50 seconds version confirming members were shouting 'voting' and the Speaker was asking them to be patient for the vote, and a report by Dawn stated that opposition leaders were chanting 'voting, voting' to call for their version of the resolution when the Foreign Minister began to address the house.
statements.support_span: The opposition in Pakistan’s Assembly was shouting “voting, voting” for passing a resolution presented by them and not “Modi, Modi”. | In the 17 minutes 50-second version of the parliamentary proceedings, it is clear that the members are shouting “voting” and not “Modi”. We can also hear the Speaker calming down the members by asking them to be patient and saying that voting will take place. | When Foreign Minister Shah Mehmood Qureshi began to address the house, opposition leaders started chanting “voting, voting” calling for the resolution presented by their side, according to the report.

statements.statement: The video originates from a Pakistan National Assembly session held on October 26 regarding a resolution against caricatures in Charlie Hebdo and remarks by the French President, where Pakistani journalist Mateen Haider confirmed that no pro-Modi slogans were raised in the parliament, noting the only mention of Modi was in a slogan against his friends, and PM Narendra Modi's name was mentioned during the proceedings because the ruling party accused the opposition of colluding with him.
statements.support_span: With the help of appropriate keywords, we found that the video is from Pakistan’s National Assembly session held on October 26. A resolution was passed in the Assembly against the “blasphemous” caricature carried by French satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo and the recent remarks made by French President Emmanuel Macron on Islam. | AFWA also contacted Mateen Haider, a senior journalist from Pakistan who confirmed that no slogans in support of the Indian government were raised in Pakistan’s parliament. “The only slogan that was raised mentioning Modi was ‘'Modi ka jo yaar hai, Gaddar hai gaddar hai' (Modi's friends are traitors). There were no pro-Modi slogans raised in the parliament,” Haider confirmed. | The report also mentions that PM Narendra Modi’s name cropped up during the proceedings when the ruling party accused the opposition of colluding with the Indian PM.

silver.justification: The evidence indicates that the viral video is a misinterpretation of parliamentary proceedings from October 26. Rather than chanting 'Modi, Modi', members of the Pakistani National Assembly were actually shouting 'voting, voting' to demand a vote on a resolution regarding Charlie Hebdo and remarks by the French President. A longer version of the video and reports from Dawn confirm the 'voting' chants, while journalist Mateen Haider clarified that no pro-Modi slogans were raised; the only mention of the Indian PM was in a slogan criticizing his associates. The name 'Modi' appeared in the session only because the ruling party accused the opposition of colluding with him.
